description: How to reproduce SAS's legacy RANUNI/RANNOR pseudo-random stream so seeded splits and simulations match a SAS baseline exactly.

ranuni_stream.title: SAS RANUNI is a prime-modulus multiplicative congruential generator (m=2^31-1, a=397204094); reproduce it exactly for seeded parity.
rule: The legacy RANUNI(seed) stream is s_{k+1} = (a * s_k) mod m with a = 397204094 and m = 2^31 - 1 (2147483647); the uniform draw is s_{k+1} / m.
A fixed POSITIVE integer seed makes the stream reproducible; a non-positive seed makes SAS use the time of day (not reproducible) and should be rejected in a port.
RANNOR (normal) draws are derived from this same uniform stream, so matching RANUNI is the prerequisite for matching any RANNOR-based simulation.
numpy's default RNG (PCG64) is a completely different algorithm; to match a SAS baseline exactly you must implement the SAS recurrence, not seed numpy.
Newer code that uses RAND('UNIFORM') with CALL STREAMINIT uses the Mersenne-Twister family, which is different again; check which generator the SAS baseline used before porting.
pitfalls: Seeding np.random with the SAS seed does NOT reproduce SAS draws — the algorithms differ.
A non-positive seed in SAS is time-based; a port that treats it as reproducible will silently diverge.
Order of draws matters: consume the stream in the same sequence SAS does (e.g. one draw per observation, in data-step order).

code: """Reproduce the legacy SAS RANUNI uniform(0,1) stream."""
